item.title: Dashboard
item.description:
A graphical dashboard for the engine — containers, images, volumes and a wctr terminal — built with go-widgets, running in the browser on the same engine and API as wctr. Every action shows the wctr command it stands for. This is dashboard v0.2.0, which runs on engine v0.5.0.

What it does

  • The Start, Stop and Restart buttons use the engine’s /start, /stop and /restart, and show the matching wctr start|stop|restart NAME line in the footer and in the terminal. Stop returns once the container has exited.
  • The status bar shows the storage, from GET /system/df (for example IndexedDB 2MB of 1GB (persistent)).
  • Volumes, live events and stats appear automatically once the engine serves them.

Live demo: https://go-wasmcontainers.github.io/dashboard/. Source: go-wasmcontainers/dashboard.

The terminal widget

The terminal in the dashboard is the Terminal widget that go-widgets/toolkit v0.342.0 adds: a subset of xterm, safe for untrusted output. It has no reply channel (nothing the output prints is ever sent back), and OSC, DCS and APC sequences are dropped.

Limitations

  • The Volumes view and the live events appear once the engine serves them; the dashboard polls every 2 seconds until the engine serves /events.
  • The standalone demo keeps its state in memory: nothing persists across a reload. Persistence comes when the dashboard becomes the playground’s main UI (planned).
  • Browsers keep Ctrl-W, Ctrl-T and Ctrl-N, so the terminal cannot use them.
  • dashboard.wasm is 20 MB uncompressed.
  • The end-to-end tests have not yet been run in Firefox.

Next

The dashboard is planned to become the playground’s main UI. That has not happened: the playground is still the terminal page.
